submitted.rationale: Index 175 (Fe0.61 Ni0.215 V0.175) had the highest measured photocurrent: 7.7e-7 A. Higher-Fe compositions gave more photocurrent than the FeVO4-like one. MEGNet band gaps for Fe-containing oxide phases (HSE about 2.75 eV) are below the 3.2 eV photon energy, which fits Fe-rich films absorbing the light.

rejected.reason: FeVO4-like Fe:V=1:1 composition gave 4.1e-7 A, well below the Fe-rich compositions
Fe-rich corner gave 7.0e-7 A, slightly below its neighbour 175

consultations.verdict: Support: MEGNet HSE gaps ~2.75 eV for Fe-containing oxide phases (mp-504509, mp-19770) are below the 3.2 eV photon energy, so Fe-V-rich compositions should absorb; index 144 (Fe0.41 V0.41 Ni0.18) sits near FeVO4 stoichiometry, a known photoanode.

Weakly supportive / mostly uninformative: the GLLB gap for mp-19770 (0.89 eV) is not quantitative, but the HSE gaps for Fe oxides (~2.77 eV) mean Fe-rich films absorb 3.2 eV light. Measuring the Fe-rich corner (index 49, Fe0.62) tests the Fe-content gradient relative to 144.

Supportive: PBE gap for mp-504509 is 2.08 eV (HSE 2.75), well below 3.2 eV, so Fe-rich vanadate/oxide mixtures absorb. The measurements show Fe-rich (49: 7.0e-7 A) beats FeVO4-like (144: 4.1e-7 A), so I'm staying near the high-Fe edge: index 175 (Fe0.61, V0.175, Ni0.215).
